messages:
morgan: FYI the release publish job failed because typegen bumped the client semver from a generator-only reorder. publish blocked. :grimacing:
ci-bot: publish-job-7489 failed: changelog.semver_check failed. Detected version diff 2.0.7 -> 2.1.0 (expected patch). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/7489
elaine: i'm on it. earlier today i noticed the sample app auth/retry tests flaked and we retriggered the build. that build uses the freshly built SDK which seems to have produced a different property ordering in the generated types.
josh: property ordering flip is likely the culprit. typegen's differ treats reorders as potential minor if not normalized. did the spec actually change or just ordering?
elaine: spec unchanged semantically. backend PR reordered two optional fields (nonbreaking). typegen currently preserves input order which caused regenerate to reorder fields relative to prior generated output.
pat: quick note on flow: publish pipeline runs build -> integration tests (sample app) -> regenerate types -> semver/changelog check -> publish. Using the just-built SDK in the integration step creates a circular dependency: rebuild changes shapes -> regen -> semver bump.
morgan: two asks: 1) can we avoid using the fresh SDK artifact during the publish gating so a flaky test doesn't retrigger regen? 2) long-term: can typegen have a stable-sort pass so these reorders don't cause false semver bumps?
josh: for (1) yes, we can pin the integration test step to the last tagged SDK or run tests against the compiled artifact only, not the pre-release. i'll draft a pipeline patch. for (2) i've been pushing a stable sort normalization. it will dedupe ordering noise before diffing.
elaine: opening a small PR on typegen to run a deterministic property/enum sort prior to diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/typegen/pull/462. includes unit tests and an opt-in flag.
ci-bot: artifacts for job 7489: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/publish/7489. changelog diff generated by typegen v0.18.3: `- 2.0.7 -> 2.1.0`
pat: short-term workaround: add a release label `publish/regen-doc-only` that allows a maintainer to override semver guard when the diff is only ordering/whitespace in generated code. i'll add the label and update the release playbook.
morgan: sounds good. also please add a note in the release guide and tag releases channel if this override is used. we need an audit trail.;josh: i'll open the pipeline MR today to pin sample app tests to latest tag. ETA: EOD.
elaine: PR #462 will add the normalized diff output. i'll also add a check in the generator CI that bumps no semver when only ordering changes are present.
pat: adding a CI alert: if auth/retry tests fail in publish flow, stop and notify, don't auto-rebuild and regen.
morgan: great. if we can merge both PRs tomorrow morning we should unblock the weekend release. thanks team. :thumbsup:
